cells.tense: You are still here, still hoping, and the hope has not gone thin.
cells.ask: Give the one thing worth continuing the next hour, and only that hour.
cells.core:
You keep returning to something whose result you can't see yet. The return itself is the strength. Not certainty, not a sign — you do the unglamorous part, show up again the next day, and the hoping holds because it keeps being practiced. Plenty of people can hold on for a while. You've turned it into a habit, and the habit is doing its work.

This is also where it stays clean. Add a little, pull back a little, without making a ceremony of it, so the effort matches what's actually there today. Holding on like this costs one plain look at the load before you pick it up. Nothing has to be repaired first. The continuing itself is the thing; it was not the delay before the thing.
cells.sheetLine: You keep going on a hope that hasn't been confirmed yet.

cells.tense: You are bracing against something ahead that has not happened yet.
cells.ask: Leave one open question alone for a day and do nothing to prepare for it.
cells.core:
Steady persistence looks like this when it's working: you read the day in front of you, take the step that's actually there, and let the rest wait until it exists. The hoping holds its shape without straining toward a result, and the strength lasts because it isn't being spent on tomorrow as well.

What's happening instead is a reach past the present. You're forcing an ending into shape before it's ready — checking, pushing, rehearsing the version where it fails. The persistence is real and it is aimed too far forward, which is where the strength is leaking. Pulling the aim back to today is the whole repair. Nothing about the hope needs to change.
cells.sheetLine: You're pushing for a result before it's ready to arrive.

cells.tense: You are standing at a door that is already behind you.
cells.ask: Give one living thing you're part of a little attention today, then leave it be.
cells.core:
When the hoping feeds itself, it looks like this: you tend something real, give it a bit of care, and the care doesn't exhaust you or turn into hanging on. You can hold room for a thing to grow without standing over it. The continuing has a source because something is actually being looked after, and it keeps giving back.

That source has gone quiet. You carry the hoping but you've stopped acting like it's yours to look after. Nothing gets added and nothing gets let go, so the middle goes flat and the door stays half-open behind you. Getting back doesn't run through pushing harder or feeling more. It runs through one small act of care for something alive, small enough to finish today.
cells.sheetLine: The hope is still there, but you've stopped tending it.

cells.tense: You are already doing this, and you keep describing it as though it were happening to you.
cells.ask: Say out loud or write down one thing you keep going on, and call it yours.
cells.core:
When this is owned, it sounds ordinary: you keep showing up, adjust when the situation shifts, come back the next day — and you'd say that's you doing it, without turning it into a speech. Put a name on the doing and it can be trusted, rested, and picked up again on purpose. Left unnamed, it looks like something that happened to you.

The name is missing from the account. You go on through all of it, then talk as if circumstances were carrying you. That isn't modesty. It's a settled habit of leaving yourself out of your own story, which makes it harder to trust what you do and easier to feel shoved around. There is no more effort to add here. Only the admitting that the continuing is yours.
cells.sheetLine: You already keep going. You just haven't claimed it.
